- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate — apply downward bias of 3–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile or mixed — use sentiment average over last 5 days to adjust forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion — if recent 7-day average is > 75, forecast should not exceed 78 unless sentiment > 0.4.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays correction — add 1–2 day lag to forecast adjustment if sentiment shifts > 0.3 upward.
